run.procedureSummary:
Step 1 Charge: add each stage's cycle input to its charge; no rating cap.
Step 2 Shunts: sweep positions 1 to 6 in order; if charge > rating, set to rating and add the excess to the next position before that one is checked (cascades in one pass); position 6's excess goes to ground (loss tally).
Step 3 Comparators: on post-shunt charge, evaluate each stage once: CLEAR with charge >= upper becomes ASSERTED; ASSERTED with charge <= lower becomes CLEAR; otherwise hold. Log each change (cycle, position, before, after).
Step 4 Leak/feedback: compute all six amounts from the post-comparator charges and the states just set, then apply simultaneously. CLEAR: floor(charge/4) to ground. ASSERTED: floor(charge/2) moved to the previous position (toward source); position 1's ASSERTED feedback goes to ground. No rating cap.
Step 5 Breaker: if the six-stage total is strictly > 38, every stage keeps floor(charge/2) and the remainder goes to ground; at <= 38 nothing happens.
All ground amounts (shunt-6 excess, CLEAR leak, stage-1 feedback, breaker remainder) are added to the loss tally. Repeat for cycles 1-5.

openPoints.assumption: All rounded down (floor) on whole units; the breaker's ground amount is charge minus floor(charge/2), so odd charges lose the extra unit.

run.procedureSummary:
Applied each cycle's five steps in order, each step finishing on all six forms before the next:
1. Pour: add that cycle's units to each form. Capacity is not checked at this step.
2. Overtop: go from form 1 to form 6 in order. Any excess over capacity moves into the next form, and the form is left at exactly its capacity. Excess that a form has just received counts when that form is reached, so it can cascade. Form 6's excess goes to the waste pit and onto the loss tally.
3. State check, on the contents after overtop: a GREEN form at or above its upper mark becomes HOT, and a HOT form at or below its lower mark becomes GREEN (equal to the mark counts). Each form is checked once per cycle, so it changes state at most once. Each change is logged as (cycle, position, before, after).
4. Bleed/evaporation: all six amounts are computed from the contents after the state check, using the new states, and then applied together. A GREEN form loses floor(q/4) to evaporation, which goes on the loss tally. A HOT form sends floor(q/2) to the form before it (form i to form i-1); form 1's bleed is waste. There is no capacity cap at this step.
5. Washout: total the six forms. If the total is strictly over 38, each form keeps floor(q/2), the remainder goes on the loss tally, and the cycle is recorded. Otherwise nothing happens.
The loss tally starts at 0 and collects pit overflow, evaporation, form 1's bleed and washout losses.

run.procedureSummary:
Applied in cycles 1-5, steps in order. Each step finishes on all six crucibles before the next one starts.
1 Charge: add each crucible's charge for the cycle to its melt. Contents may sit above capacity until step 2.
2 Overflow: walk positions 1 to 6. Any excess over capacity is added to the next crucible before that crucible is checked, so overflow cascades, and the crucible is left exactly at capacity. Excess from crucible 6 goes to the slag pit (loss tally).
3 State check on the contents after overflow: BASE with quantity >= upper mark becomes SUPERHEATED. SUPERHEATED with quantity <= lower mark becomes BASE. Otherwise the state is unchanged, with at most one change per crucible per cycle.

5 Global reset: if the total of all six is strictly > 38, each crucible becomes floor(q/2), the removed melt q - floor(q/2) goes to slag, and the cycle is noted. At 38 or below nothing happens.
